description: Signed finite costs do not prevent top expected utility when a single rewarded policy has positive prior and a positively weighted act. With two complementary incompatible reward policies, both with positive priors, every probability mixture attains top. Zero prior/action controls are finite, and opposing infinite utility contributions produce undefined expectation. The previous nonnegative mixture certificate is reused, not counted as a new result. Conditional mathematical working reconstruction, not an attributed historical claim or truth-root discharge.
